notes.decision: The character ϩⲁ appears three times around the chapter heading (line 3 alone, line 5 start, line 5 end). Treated as decorative section/title markers analogous to the >· ·< glyphs flanking the page header. Preserved untranslated in both Coptic and English fields.

ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲁⲧϥ̄ qualitative substantive 'the chosen one' is treated here as collective referring to the four elements as the elect substance. The copular ⲡⲉ following resumes the four elements as subject: 'these four chosen elements — it (the elect substance) is from the beginning.'

ⲡⲃⲱϣ rendered 'nakedness' from verb ⲃⲱϣ 'be naked, stripped' (Lycopolitan reflex of ⲃⲱⲱϣ). The kephalaion's central technical term: each defilement's 'nakedness' (= what is revealed when it is stripped away by purifying agency) is itself the next worse defilement in the chain. This produces the recursive series bond → wrath → flow/desire → bitterness → heat → flesh → gloom → severity → ... totaling twelve strippings (line 28).

Parsed as ⲃⲁϣ-ⲥ̄ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ 'she-strips of-them' + ⲛ̄ⲥ-ⲕⲁⲁ-ϩ 'and-she-leaves-it' — the fire (fem.) strips the defilements off the descending elements and leaves the residue in the body. The ⲙⲙⲁϩ object is plural (the defilements/garments), but the resumptive ⲕⲁⲁϩ uses 3sg referring to the collective 'nakedness.'

Greek loanword ⲍⲣⲉⲩⲙⲁ = ῥεῦμα 'flow, current.' The phrase 'the flow of strippings naked itself' identifies the act/medium of stripping (ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ) with a flowing-substance — the released defilement-fluid that wells up as the counsels (ⲙⲟⲩⲗⲉⲩⲉ) strip themselves out of one another. The intensive ⲍⲱⲱⲩ ('itself, even') marks the identity: the flow IS the stripping IS the desire.

Translated 'severity' from ⲛⲁϣⲧ- 'hard, severe' + ⲙⲏⲉ 'truth' (cf. ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϣⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉ 'strictness-of-truth' in glossary). Here in the negative-correspondence chain, the term names the harsh/cruel severity that emerges when gloom is stripped away — moral hardness without mercy.

'The winds of shame' — plural ⲛⲧⲏⲩ 'winds' + ϣⲓⲡⲉ 'shame.' Cosmological-affective category: shame manifested as wind-like emanations. Continues the elemental-correspondential register where each defilement has an elemental vehicle (heat, flow, winds).

The word completed by editorial restoration [ⲙⲓⲏ] is uncertain. Could represent an ordinal in the twelve-stripping series, or a technical term such as 'midst' (ⲙⲏⲏⲧⲉ) or a specific cosmic locus. Translation marked as uncertain.

Translated 'stand fast' — variant of the standard idiom ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ (in glossary) using ⲱⲍⲉ (Lyc. for ⲱϩⲉ 'stand') with the directional ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'on the feet of.' Same semantic field of upright establishment.
Translated 'the New Man' — Lyc. variant of ⲡⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ (in glossary as the Pauline καινὸς ἄνθρωπος). The vowel-form ⲃϥ̄ⲣⲉ for ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ shows the same root ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ 'new' confirmed in vocabulary.

Translated ⲥⲁⲡ here as 'time/season' (per glossary 'time, appointed turn'), not as the homonym 'sword' attested in K.81. Context (the moment when the elect reach their first rest) demands the temporal sense.

Translated 'transmigration' — Greek loanword μετάγγισμός 'decanting, transfusion,' the standard technical term in Manichaean texts for the transmigration of sinful souls from body to body, paralleling ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲗⲗⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'exchange/transmutation' in glossary.

Translated tentatively as 'a sentencing' — the form with double overlines suggests an abbreviated Greek-derived term, possibly a contracted 'judgment' or 'fixed-decree.' Could alternatively be ⲟⲩⲇⲩⲛⲁⲙⲓⲥ 'a power' or ⲟⲩⲧⲛⲟ 'a manner.' The pairing 'transmigration with X' fits Manichaean eschatology of judgment-driven metempsychosis.
